As the event takes place during the Clone Wars, which ended in [[19 BBY]] according to ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'', Din Djarin must have been born sometime prior to the war's conclusion in 19 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]]. |death= |species=[[Human]]{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 1: The Mandalorian}} |gender=[[Gender|Male]]{{Databank|the-mandalorian|The Mandalorian}} |pronouns=He/him |height=1.8 [[meter]]s{{BustCollectionCite|80|Character}} {{C|5[[Foot|ft]] 11in}}''[[Star Wars: Character Encyclopedia, Updated and Expanded Edition]]'' |mass= |hair=[[Color|Dark brown]] |feathers= |eyes=Brown |skin=Tan |cyber= |families=*[[The Tribe]] *[[Clan Mudhorn]] |parents=*A [[Din Djarin's father|father]] *A [[Din Djarin's mother|mother]] |partners= |siblings= |children=[[Din Grogu]] {{C|adoptive son}}{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 24: The Return}} |affiliation=*[[Mandalorian]]s **[[Death Watch]]{{GentleGiantCite|set=Mini Busts|pack=Death Watch|altlink=https://www.entertainmentearth.com/product/star-wars-mandalorian-deathwatch-16-scale-minibust-diamond-select-showcase-previews-exclusive/dc84340}} **[[Children of the Watch]]{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 11: The Heiress}} *[[Bounty Hunters' Guild]] *[[Ranzar Malk's crew]] *[[Fett gotra]]{{BOBF|Chapter 6: From the Desert Comes a Stranger}} *[[New Republic]] {{C|independent contractor}} |masters=[[Din Djarin's teacher|Din Djarin's master]] |apprentices=Din Grogu }} {{Quote|I can bring you in warm, or I can bring you in cold.|Din Djarin|audio=Djarin-WarmorCold-TMS1C1.flac|}} '''Din Djarin''', also known as "'''the Mandalorian'''," or simply "'''Mando'''," was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] [[Mandalorian]] [[Mandalorian warrior|warrior]] during the [[New Republic Era|era]] of the [[New Republic]]. With his [[Din Djarin's armor|Mandalorian armor]], [[IB-94 blaster|IB-94]] [[The Mandalorian's IB-94 blaster pistol|blaster pistol]], [[Amban phase-pulse blaster|Amban sniper rifle]], and distinctive [[beskar]] [[helmet]], Djarin was both well-equipped and enigmatic—a stranger whose past was shrouded in mystery to others. An orphan [[Homeworld|born]] on [[Aq Vetina]] in the waning years of the [[Galactic Republic]], he was raised on [[Concordia]] as a [[foundling]] by the [[Children of the Watch]], an orthodox [[Religion|religious sect]] that had broken off from mainstream Mandalorian society. He vowed to walk the [[Way of the Mandalore]], swearing to never again reveal his face to another living being, and eventually joined [[the Tribe]], which operated in a [[Nevarro Mandalorian covert|secret covert]] on the [[planet]] [[Nevarro]]. After the [[Battle of Jakku|fall]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], Djarin made a reputation for himself as a [[Bounty hunter|member]] of the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild]]. Far from the authority of the New Republic, he traveled across the galaxy's [[Outer Rim Territories]] in his personal [[ST-70 M-111 Razor Crest series|ST-70 Assault Ship]], the ''[[Razor Crest]],'' collecting [[Bounty|bounties]] and delivering them, warm or cold, to [[Guild Master]] [[Greef Karga]]. Djarin became battle-hardened, a man of few words, and a formidable hunter in an increasingly dangerous [[The galaxy|galaxy]]. In [[9 ABY]], Djarin was [[Hunt for Grogu|hired]] on Nevarro by a [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|Imperial faction]] to [[Mission to Arvala-7|acquire]] a mysterious asset. The Mandalorian tracked the bounty to the world [[Arvala-7]] and discovered that his quarry was a [[Force-sensitive]] [[Youngling|infant]] belonging to the same [[Yoda's species|species]] as [[Jedi]] [[Grand Master]] [[Yoda]]. A paternal bond soon formed between Djarin and the child, who the hunter later learned to be named [[Din Grogu|Grogu]]. The outwardly-emotionless Mandalorian could not bring himself to surrender the youngling to the Imperials and [[Incident on Nevarro|absconded]] with the child, bringing him into conflict with the brutal [[warlord]], [[Moff]] [[Gideon]]. Djarin, alongside Karga, former [[shock trooper]] [[Carasynthia Dune|Cara Dune]], and others, went on to drive the Moff's forces out of [[Nevarro City]] and reunite with [[the Armorer]], the leader of his covert and staunch upholder of the [[Mandalorian Creed]]. She christened Djarin and Grogu as a [[Clan Mudhorn|clan of two]], commanding the Mandalorian to care for the child until he could deliver him to the remaining [[Jedi Knight]]s, few in number and scattered across space. Djarin and Grogu scoured the galaxy in search of the fabled masters of [[the Force]], battling vicious foes and forging new alliances. These adventures saw Djarin cross paths with several faces that challenged his notions of what it meant to be a Mandalorian; these included [[Cobb Vanth]], a [[Tatooine|Tatooinian]] [[marshal]] who used scavenged [[Boba Fett's armor|beskar armor]] to defend a [[Freetown|small town]]; [[Bo-Katan Kryze]], a [[princess]] of [[Mandalore]] who laid claim to the [[Mandalore (title)|planet's unoccupied throne]]; and [[Boba Fett]], a legendary bounty hunter and Mandalorian [[Cloning|clone]] who sought to reclaim his legacy. After encountering the wandering [[ronin]] [[Ahsoka Tano]] and fighting in a series of skirmishes against the [[Imperial Remnant]], the Mandalorian and his allies eventually [[Assault on Moff Gideon's cruiser|captured]] Moff Gideon and meet with [[Luke Skywalker]], a [[Jedi Master]] that promised to train Grogu as his [[Padawan|apprentice]]. Breaking his vows to the Creed, Djarin removed his helmet as he bid farewell, letting his ward see his face for the first time. Having defeated Gideon in combat, Djarin had inadvertently claimed ownership of the Moff's weapon, the [[Darksaber]], a mythic [[lightsaber]] that identified whosoever wielded it as the leader of the Mandalorian people. Reluctant to rule but unable to relinquish the ceremonial blade, Djarin returned to the Armorer, who branded him an apostate for removing his helmet. Djarin went on to fight alongside Boba Fett in the [[Battle of Mos Espa]] on Tatooine and soon reunited with Grogu, who had chosen to abandon his Jedi training in favor of staying with the Mandalorian. Seeking to regain his status as a Child of the Watch, Djarin [[Mission to the Living Waters|ventured]] into the [[Mines of Mandalore]] and bathed in the [[Living Waters]], renewing himself in the eyes of the Armorer. During his quest, Djarin was disarmed by a [[Cyborg mech|being]] that was later slain by Kryze, a sequence of events that placed ownership of the Darksaber in her hands. Uniting their disparate Mandalorian sects, Kryze and Djarin led a [[Liberation of Mandalore|reconquest]] of Mandalore, freeing the planet from the Imperial Remnant and killing Moff Gideon. With their enemy defeated, the Mandalorian and Grogu settled into a [[Clan Mudhorn homestead|quiet cabin]] on Nevarro where they chose to live peacefully, until such time that their allies in the New Republic called on them to hunt down more rogue Imperial warlords. [[Standard year|Years]] later, Djarin and Grogu worked with the [[Anzellan Droidsmiths]] to [[Mission to Nevarro's lava tubes|recover]] warheads under the surface of Nevarro. Djarin later assisted [[Garazeb Orrelios]] in [[Attack on Barro's Imperial remnant|hunting]] the Imperial warlord [[Barro]] on [[Phostera]], ultimately killing him after a fierce pursuit despite the New Republic's preference to capture him alive. Rewarded with a [[Razor Crest 2.0|new ''Razor Crest'']], Djarin accepted a [[Mission to Shakari|mission]] from Colonel [[Ward]] to rescue [[Rotta]] the Hutt in exchange for information on the elusive Imperial [[Commander]] [[Janu Coin|Coin]]. On [[Shakari]], he discovered Rotta had become a renowned gladiator and was unwilling to return to the [[The Twins|Hutt Twins]], believing they sought his death. After fighting alongside Rotta in a deadly arena, Djarin learned that the local [[crime lord]] Janu was in fact Commander Coin, and captured the Imperial leader with Orrelios' help. Djarin delivered Coin to the New Republic and returned to Nevarro. After arranging Rotta's safe escape, Djarin and the [[Anzellan]] [[Droidsmith]] [[Minch]] were [[Ambush on the Clan Mudhorn cabin|captured]] by the bounty hunter [[Embo]] and delivered to the Twins, but [[Rescue of Din Djarin|escaped]] imprisonment with Grogu and the Anzellan's aid. After recovering from [[dragonsnake]] [[Poison|venom]], he led an attack on the Hutt Palace, rescued Rotta, and battled Embo and the Twins. Having discovered the Hutt's collaboration with the Imperial Remnant, New Republic forces joined in [[Battle of Nal Hutta (Din Djarin)|battle over Nal Hutta]], destroying the palace. Following the mission, Rotta chose to remain with the New Republic, while Djarin and Grogu departed aboard the ''Razor Crest 2.0'' to continue their travels.
